scope: This file defines the machine: the console hardware, the jobs its FPGA performs and the behaviour its BIOS exposes. Implementations of the machine are the physical console, the HTML5 emulator's machine model and the Analogue Pocket core. Emulator-only features (ROM hack maker, MSX porting tools, Lab composite, merge report, the app's Debug tab, filters, FM dual-run capture, save states) are not part of the machine and are listed separately in SuperSega_v7_Reconciliation.md.

glossary.register_banks: The VDP register-write command byte is 10bbnnnn. "bank1 R3" means register 3 of bank 1, written with bb = 01. Banks 1-3 are reachable only while XRB is set.
glossary.XRB: Extended Register Banks: Feature Enable A (bank 0 R15) bit 5. While it is clear, bits 5-4 of a register-write command are ignored as on stock hardware, and the bank 1-3 registers keep their values but have no effect (Feature Enable B and C read as 0 to the hardware).
glossary.Feature_Enable_A_B_C: The three opt-in registers: A = bank 0 R15, B = bank 1 R2, C = bank 1 R7. All 0 at reset.
glossary.TH_TR: Controller-port pins: TR is button 2; TH is the light-gun / multiplexing line. Both can be outputs, set through port $3F.
glossary.ESAT: Extended Sprite Attribute Table: per-sprite flip, priority, size, magnification, early clock and palette.
glossary.unique_cell: A mode with 1024 tiles, so every cell of the 32x24 screen can have its own tile.
glossary.AEL: Auto-Enhancement Layer: the optional boosts for stock software (see enhancement_layer).
glossary.bus_synchroniser: FPGA logic that holds the CPU (Z80 WAIT) until the VDP can accept an access, needed when turbo runs the CPU faster than the VDP.
glossary.SDSC: A debug-console convention used by Master System homebrew (ports $FC/$FD).

v7_changes: Port $00 is decoded in Super Sega mode as well as Game Gear mode. v6 said GG mode only, but the Golden Axe conversion plan reverts Ax Battler's GG2SMS Start patch and relies on the stock $00 read, and the emulator already decoded it in both modes. Format corrected: bits 5-0 read 0 (the emulator returned 1s, so bit 5 reported PAL).
Ports $01-$05 (Game Gear serial/EXT link) listed explicitly for GG and Super Sega modes; v6 named the serial link under input.multiplayer but gave no ports.
$3E bit 2 scope specified: controller decode only; not on Game Gear; not $F2 or Super Sega's $F0-$FF.

Read values of the Super Sega registers inside $07-$16 and $F0-$FA specified. The emulator answered every read in $07-$16 from the controller mirror, so the math result, slot readback and multitap detection could not be read.

Debug unit port reads: in the stock modes $FB-$FF read as on the stock machine (the controller mirror; $FF on the Game Gear), and the debug unit answers reads only in Super Sega mode, which therefore decodes $F0-$FF fully. Writes reach the debug unit in every mode, as before. The emulator answered $FB-$FD reads in every mode, so stock software reading its pads at those mirror addresses saw the debug status instead.

(after the October 2026 package) port_map.mirror_scheme now gives the PSG/counter mirror across $40-$7F and the VDP mirror across $80-$BF, which both implementations decode and which the stock machines have.

(after the October 2026 package) The SG-1000, SC-3000 and SF-7000 modes have no $3E/$3F registers, so writes to $00-$3F do nothing there (port_map.mirror_scheme). The Pocket core already ignored them; the emulator let writes to $07-$3F change its I/O control value.

(after the October 2026 package) Port map corrected to match the Technical Reference and both implementations: the PSG is written at $7E as well as $7F (v6 named only $7F), and $C0-$DF is the controller mirror unless the SK-1100 keyboard is live, when the PPI answers there (v6 named only the PPI).

(after the October 2026 package) Writes to $07-$16 and to VDP bank 0 R11-R15 stated to take effect only in Super Sega mode (port_map.mode_scope, vdp_registers.bank_0_scope), as both implementations do. Q1 and port_map.open_risk now name the case at risk: old code running in Super Sega mode that writes a $3E/$3F mirror address in $06-$16. They said any old title.

Native 12-bit CRAM write order specified as the Game Gear byte-latch scheme. The emulator indexed entries by byte address while advancing the address per byte, so sequential writes filled every other entry; and in Game Gear mode it treated each byte as an SMS 6-bit colour, which gave every GG title wrong colours.
$F2 readback specified, including that it works with the I/O chip disabled. The emulator returned $FF in that state, so the standard FM detection failed.

stock_behaviour section added: the CPU and VDP behaviour the emulator was corrected to follow, from the Super Mario Land DX port work (October 2026). These are the stock parts, not changes to the machine, but every implementation must follow them.
VRAM expansion control corrected: v6 gave "bank1 R3 bit 0" in memory.vram but "bank1 R2 bit 4" in video.unique_cell_mode. R2 bit 4 enables, R3 bit 0 selects.

(after the October 2026 package) Reset values written down: $3E resets to $A8 (the BIOS has handed over to the cartridge), as the Technical Reference already said, and $3F to $FF (every pin an input, level bits set), where v6 said only "low bits set". Both implementations already use these values.
Math unit register layout written down from the emulator; the divide operation is flagged as under-specified with a proposal.
Cartridge reach and save-RAM size recorded as open, with the facts that bound them.
Software detection of the machine recorded as an open question (from the SML DX port).
Modding boundary recorded: patch application while writing a card is a machine (computer mode) feature; making mods is emulator-only.

Extra-height mode bits corrected (v6 error, also in Technical Reference v2): M2 enables the extra heights; M1 then selects 224 lines and M3 selects 240. v6 had M2 and M3 swapped. Found while testing the Pocket RTL against Gearsystem and MAME. Emulator and RTL fixed.

(after the October 2026 package) Height cases written out: with M4 and M2 set, M1 and M3 both set give 192 lines (video.mode4.height_selection did not say), and Feature Enable B height 11 gives 192 lines (the Technical Reference said only "reserved"). Both implementations already do this.

Codemasters registers are at exactly $0000, $4000 and $8000, and the Korean register at exactly $A000 (Gearsystem, MAME). v6 said any address in the slot; the emulator also powered Codemasters up with banks 0,1,2 instead of the profile's 0,1,0. Both fixed.

8255 behaviour specified for both PPIs: reset state (all inputs, row 7 selected by the pull-ups), a mode word clearing port C, and bit set/reset on the keyboard PPI. The emulator selected keyboard row 0 at reset, so SG-1000 titles could not read their pads.

(after the October 2026 package) SF-7000 PPI port C bit 2 is the floppy controller's TC (terminal count) input, not the drive's: "2 FDC TC" (v6 had "2 FDD TC"). MAME sg1000.cpp ("PC2 TC signal to FDC") and the Technical Reference agree.

(after the October 2026 package) Two risks from Technical Reference v2 that v3 keeps are recorded beside the statements they qualify: VDP registers 11-15 were checked against only six commercial titles (vdp_registers.bank_0_evidence), and the keyboard's active-low polarity rests on one source that contradicts itself (input.keyboard.polarity, no longer stated as settled).

Stock behaviour extended: sprite Y wrap rule (Gearsystem/MAME), 224/240-line name table, per-line VDP event timing, PSG noise rate and 2 dB volume steps, low-port reads, TR readback and Game Gear port decoding. The emulator had the noise an octave high, a linear volume curve, the controller mirror answering $00-$3F, and no TR readback.

(after the October 2026 package) The $F2 FM detection latch answers only in Master System and Super Sega modes (stock_behaviour.io.fm_latch); the emulator answered in the Game Gear, SC-3000 and SF-7000 modes too. The package made this change without listing it here.

Review fixes: Feature Enable A bit 6 (turbo) added to the register table and its write-enable meaning stated; XRB semantics and the Feature Enable B height encoding written down; "debug unit" added to the FPGA job list (27 jobs, as the Technical Reference says); the keyboard is also live in SG-1000 mode; a glossary added for terms used throughout.

(after the October 2026 package) PAL CPU clock defined: 3.546893 MHz, as on a PAL Master System, giving 49.70 Hz frames. v6 gave only the NTSC clock. Both implementations now run PAL on it (they ran it at the NTSC clock, 50.16 Hz). The turbo frequencies are stated for the NTSC clock; PAL ones are open question Q22.

(after the October 2026 package) CPU state at hand-over to software defined (cpu.reset_state): PC $0000, SP $DFF0, interrupts disabled, interrupt mode 0. $DFF0 is where the Master System BIOS leaves SP and where the emulator and Gearsystem start; the Pocket core's CPU reset SP to $FFFF and is changed to match.
(after the October 2026 package) Cartridge wait state at 200 % written into the profile (cpu.turbo.cartridge_wait) as the Technical Reference gives it; Q12 cited it, but no profile field stated it.

enhancement_layer section added: the boosts for stock software, all off by default, with their exact behaviour (pseudo-stereo panning, auto-fire rate), and every boost limited to software in the stock modes. The emulator's pseudo-stereo silenced PSG tones 1 and 2 ($06 = $99); it now uses $DE. Its auto-fire overwrote the pad state, which left button 2 held when C was released mid-toggle.

(after the October 2026 package) The enhancement-layer design document the profile cites (SuperSega_AutoEnhancement_Layer.md, the "AEL doc") is noted as an earlier document that is not in this repository.
open_questions section added, consolidating questions from the Golden Axe conversion plan, the ROM hack maker spec and the SML DX port, with the ones v6 already answers marked resolved.

(after the October 2026 package) Q13 now gives the ESAT history as the profile records it: 2 bytes per sprite since v5, confirmed in v6 (Q4). It said v6 made the change. video.sprites.esat.v5_change now points to Q13.

(after the October 2026 package) Line interrupts in the legacy (TMS) modes recorded as open question Q15. v5 made them a Super Sega enhancement but no enable bit was ever assigned, and compatibility.sg_software said Feature Enable C enables them, which no bit does. The statements that answered the question now point to Q15.
(after the October 2026 package) Open question Q17 added: whether Feature Enable B's 224/240-line heights apply while a TMS9918 mode is selected, as both implementations do today.

(after the October 2026 package) Open question Q16 added: the register layouts of the DMA engine, PCM control, the wavetable, slot select, the VDP base registers and the window split are defined only by the emulator's implementation. vdp_registers.bank_0 R14 now gives its bit 7 (side), as the Technical Reference does.

(after the October 2026 package) The TMS9918 modes written down (video.legacy_modes: tables, transparency, sprites, status_flags) as the Pocket core implements them. The emulator was corrected to them: the lowest-numbered sprite is now drawn on top, sprites set the collision flag, colour 0 is transparent in Text and Multicolor, and R3 bits 6-0 mask the Graphics II colour index (it applied the mask shifted by five bits). video.legacy_modes.selection gives the mode bits instead of claiming real-hardware behaviour for every combination. Open questions Q18 (status bits 4-0, transparent sprites) and Q19 (several mode bits at once) added.

(after the October 2026 package) Q11 resolved by the owner: True TMS colours is on at power-on, the one exception to every boost starting off, and it also acts on Super Sega software's TMS modes. enhancement_layer.default and precedence say so. The sprite-limit boost now says what both implementations do in the TMS modes (4 -> 16); it said "4 -> 8 or 16". The stock-overflow-flag boost is stated to act in Mode 4 only.

(after the October 2026 package) The four $F2 states written out (audio.fm.audio_control.write): 0 PSG only, 1 FM only, 2 neither, 3 both. The profile said only that bits 1-0 "select the mute/enable state"; the emulator mixed both chips whatever $F2 held, so software that selected FM only still had its PSG heard. The source is MAME sms_m.cpp, not sms.cpp. Open question Q20 added: the balance of FM and PSG.

(after the October 2026 package) Open question Q21 added and decided by the owner: FM register writes at turbo could come faster than the YM2413 accepts them, so the bus synchroniser holds the CPU on $F0/$F1 until the chip is ready (cpu.turbo.fm_writes). audio.fm.write_timing gives the chip's write timing.

(after the October 2026 package) Stock-mode controller mapping decided by the owner (input.stock_mapping): the Mega Drive pad's A is button 1 and B is button 2, and Start is the Game Gear's Start or, through Start = Pause, the Pause button; Start = Pause is now on at power-on, the second boost that starts on. The documents said only that the pad gives B and C with TH high, as a Mega Drive pad does; the emulator already used A and B.
(after the October 2026 package) Open question Q22 added: the turbo frequencies in PAL. Both implementations run the turbo steps as percentages of the PAL clock (cpu.turbo.clock_generation).
v5_changes: SG-series capability recovery: features the TMS9918 had and the SMS/GG Mode 4 VDP dropped are restored.
Enhanced legacy modes - TMS modes 0-3 may draw from 12-bit CRAM instead of the fixed TMS palette, with the sprite-per-line limit raised and line interrupts available.
16x16 sprites RE-ATTRIBUTED to the TMS9918/SG-1000, which had them before the Master System removed them. 32x32 via magnification added.
Per-sprite early clock and per-sprite magnification added (SG had per-sprite early clock; the SMS has only a global 8-pixel shift).
Extended Sprite Attribute Table widened to 2 bytes per sprite to carry the new flags.
Text window: the window layer may render as a 40-column, 6-pixel-wide text plane, bringing SC-3000 text density into Mode 4.
1024-tile unique-cell mode, recovering the Graphics II pseudo-bitmap capability at Mode 4 colour depth.
SC-3000 keyboard support through the expansion port.
New Feature Enable C register at bank 1 R7.

sg_capability_analysis.premise: The Mode 4 VDP is not a strict superset of the TMS9918. The Master System added Mode 4 and kept the legacy modes for compatibility, but several TMS capabilities have no Mode 4 equivalent.

lost_and_recovered.tms: SAT attribute bit 7 shifts that sprite 32 px left
lost_and_recovered.mode4: reg0 bit 3 shifts ALL sprites 8 px

lost_and_recovered.tms: Mode 2: 768 patterns = every one of 32x24 cells unique (pseudo-bitmap)
lost_and_recovered.mode4: 512 tiles max, so cells must be reused

lost_and_recovered.tms: SC-3000 was a computer with a full keyboard

deliberately_not_taken.reason: Mode 4 already allows 8, and Super Sega allows 16. The TMS limit is strictly worse.
TMS sprites carry one colour each; Mode 4 sprites are 15-colour. Per-sprite colour selection is instead provided by the ESAT palette index, which gives both.
Replaced by 12-bit CRAM. The enhanced legacy modes keep the TMS structure but draw programmable colours.

detection.offset_note: The BIOS checks all three in turn; 8 KB and 16 KB ROMs carry the header lower down. v5 listed only 0x7FF0, under which every small ROM reads as headerless.

layout.+12..+13: product code, BCD, last four digits, high pair in the second byte
layout.+14: high nibble any remaining product digits, low nibble version
layout.+15: high nibble region, low nibble checksum range (commonly called the ROM size code)

detection.export_bios_note: An export SMS BIOS rejects any cartridge whose region nibble is not 4 with a software error. Region 8 software therefore will not boot on stock export hardware.

cpu.clock_standards: base_clock_hz is the NTSC clock. In PAL the CPU runs at pal_clock_hz, as on a PAL Master System, so a 313-line frame of 228 cycles per line is 49.70 Hz (at the NTSC clock it would be 50.16 Hz).
cpu.reset_state: At hand-over to software: PC $0000, SP $DFF0 (where the Master System BIOS leaves it), interrupts disabled (IFF1 = IFF2 = 0) and interrupt mode 0, as after a Z80 reset; software selects IM 1 itself.

turbo.principle: extra CPU cycles per frame; VDP/PSG/FM stay at 1x
turbo.clock_generation: FPGA PLL generates true 4.47/5.37/6.26/7.16 MHz at the NTSC clock (PAL turbo frequencies: open question Q22); VDP, PSG and FM stay at 1x
turbo.enable: Feature Enable A bit 6 - off at reset. A write to $F3 takes effect only while it is set, so unmodified SMS/GG software can never change the clock; the step stays in force until $F3 is written again.
turbo.cartridge_wait: A 250 ns cartridge ROM is fast enough up to 175 %; at 200 % each cartridge access takes one wait state (open question Q12 covers the Pocket core).
turbo.v5_error: v5 placed this on port 0x3F bits 6-4, which are the TR output levels for controller ports A and B. Any title driving TR would have changed the clock.
turbo.fm_writes: The FM chip stays at 1x. At turbo steps above 100 % the bus synchroniser holds the CPU on a write to $F0/$F1 until 12 base cycles have passed since an address write, or 84 since a data write (audio.fm.write_timing), so software written for 100 % keeps its FM music. Open question Q21, decided by the owner.

bus_synchroniser.purpose: Holds the CPU until the VDP reaches a safe access point, since the CPU clock is decoupled from the VDP under turbo.
bus_synchroniser.source: Official Sega Mark III software reference manual
bus_synchroniser.consequence: An OUTI loop of 16 T-states is free in VBLANK at any turbo step. During active video every access waits; at 200% the steady-state penalty is 42 CPU cycles per access.

height_selection.standard: M2 (R0 bit 1) enables the extra heights. With M4 and M2 set, M1 (R1 bit 4) gives 224 lines and M3 (R1 bit 3) gives 240; with both M1 and M3 set it stays 192 lines. With M2 clear, Mode 4 is 192 lines whatever M1 and M3 say. M4 is R0 bit 2.
height_selection.super_sega: additionally selectable through Feature Enable B bits 7-6
height_selection.note: Extra height modes are SMS2 features; they do not work on an SMS1. The name table becomes 32x32 rather than 32x28, and 0xD0 stops acting as a sprite-list terminator.
height_selection.v6_error: v6 gave 224 = M4 M3 M1 with M2 clear and 240 = M4 M3 M2 with M1 clear, swapping the roles of M2 and M3. Under it, the usual R0 = $36 with R1 bit 4 set stayed at 192 lines, and R0 = $04 with R1 bits 4-3 set gave 224 lines where hardware shows 192.

modes.0: Graphics I - 32x24 tiles, colour per 8-tile group
modes.1: Text - 40 columns of 6-pixel characters, no sprites
modes.2: Graphics II - 768 unique patterns, colour per 8x1 row (pseudo-bitmap)

legacy_modes.selection: Graphics I with none of M1-M3 set, Text with M1 (R1 bit 4), Graphics II with M2 (R0 bit 1), Multicolor with M3 (R1 bit 3); M4 (R0 bit 2) selects Mode 4. Several of M1-M3 together: open question Q19.

cram_colour.effect: The 16 fixed TMS palette entries are replaced by CRAM entries 0-15, giving 12-bit programmable colour from a 4096-colour space while the mode's tile and colour-table structure is unchanged.
cram_colour.purpose: This is to SG-1000 software what the Mode 4 hybrid is to SMS software: the same picture structure, freed from a fixed palette. An SG-1000 conversion gains full colour authority without touching its graphics layout.
cram_colour.default: off - legacy modes use the authentic fixed TMS palette

sprite_limit.effect: raises the legacy per-scanline sprite limit from 4 to the Mode 4 limit in force (8 or 16)
sprite_limit.purpose: the TMS 4-sprite limit is the single worst constraint in SG-1000 software

line_interrupts.effect: VDP register 10 line interrupts, an SMS addition, while running legacy modes (proposed in v5)
line_interrupts.purpose: raster splits and mid-screen effects in SG-1000-structured software
line_interrupts.enable: OPEN - no enable bit is defined, and whether the line counter runs in the legacy modes is undecided (open question Q15)

legacy_modes.tables: Base addresses as on the SG-1000: name table R2 x $400, colour table R3 x $40, pattern table R4 x $800, sprite attributes R5 x $80, sprite patterns R6 x $800. In Graphics II, R4 bit 2 and R3 bit 7 pick the half of VRAM for the pattern and colour tables, and R4 bits 1-0 and R3 bits 6-0 mask the pattern and colour index, so the thirds of the screen can share tables.
legacy_modes.transparency: Colour 0 is transparent in every TMS mode, Text and Multicolor included: the backdrop (R7 bits 3-0) shows through.
legacy_modes.sprites: 32 sprites of 4 bytes (Y, X, pattern, attribute: bit 7 early clock, 32 pixels left; bits 3-0 colour), 8x8 or 16x16 (R1 bit 1), magnified by R1 bit 0; none in Text mode. Y = $D0 ends the list. A sprite starts on line Y+1, or Y+1-256 when Y+1 is 225 or more (Gearsystem: 224; the two differ only for Y = $DF, off a 192-line screen either way). Four per line as stock. When sprites overlap, the lowest-numbered is drawn on top. A transparent sprite counts towards the limit but draws nothing; neither implementation lets it take part in collisions, as in Gearsystem, and whether it should is open question Q18.
legacy_modes.status_flags: Status bit 6 is set by a fifth sprite on a displayed line, and status bit 5 when pixels of two drawn sprites meet on the screen; both when the line is drawn, not at the Mode 4 event times. What status bits 4-0 read is open question Q18.
legacy_modes.source: TMS9918A Data Manual (Texas Instruments); Gearsystem (Video.cpp, RenderBackgroundTMS9918 and RenderSpritesTMS9918), which the emulator matches on the Pocket core's TMS test ROMs

sprites.size_16x16_source: TMS9918 / SG-1000 - present on the SG series, removed on the Master System, restored here

early_clock.per_sprite: ESAT byte 0 bit 5 - shifts that sprite 32 pixels left
early_clock.global: register 0 bit 3 - shifts all sprites 8 pixels left, unchanged
early_clock.purpose: lets individual sprites enter and leave the left edge smoothly; the SMS could only shift the whole sprite plane

esat.v5_change: widened from 1 byte to 2 to carry magnify and early clock. The v4 single-byte layout is superseded; the emulator still implements a 1-byte layout while Feature Enable C bit 4 is clear (open question Q13).

collision.extended: per-sprite hit bitmaps at bank1 R6 base

text_mode.effect: the window plane renders as 40 columns of 6-pixel-wide characters instead of 32 columns of 8-pixel tiles
text_mode.colours: bank1 R9 - bits 3-0 foreground palette index, bits 7-4 background palette index
text_mode.purpose: 25 percent more text per line for dialogue, menus and status panels, while the main playfield stays in Mode 4 with scrolling, sprites and 12-bit colour. Recovers SC-3000 text density without a whole-screen mode change.

unique_cell_mode.effect: name table bit 15 becomes tile index bit 9, giving 1024 tiles - enough for all 32x24 = 768 screen cells to be unique
unique_cell_mode.trade: the extended-palette index narrows from 4 bits to 3 (8 palettes instead of 16) because bit 15 is reassigned
unique_cell_mode.source: TMS9918 Mode 2, whose 768 unique patterns made every cell independent
unique_cell_mode.purpose: recovers the Graphics II pseudo-bitmap capability at Mode 4 colour depth: full-screen unique imagery with 16-colour tiles instead of two colours per 8x1 row

color_system.legacy_mode_use: With bank1 R7 bit 0 set, TMS modes index CRAM entries 0-15 in place of the fixed TMS palette.

power_on_state.palette_written_flags: 16 flags; an unwritten palette aliases to palette (index AND 1)

native.addressing: Byte-addressed as on the Game Gear: a write to an even CRAM address is held in a latch and the write to the following odd address stores both bytes of the entry (entry = address >> 1). 64 bytes for 32 entries; 512 bytes for 256 entries when extended CRAM is on.

color_system.game_gear_mode: Game Gear mode uses the native byte-addressed scheme over 64 bytes.

bank_0.0-10: stock SMS VDP, including the M1-M4 mode bits
bank_0.12: Extended Sprite Attribute Table Base (now 128 bytes)
bank_0.14: Window Y Split; bit 7 selects side
bank_0.15: Feature Enable A - bit0 CRAM native, bit1 line-scroll H, bit2 window, bit3 ESAT, bit4 16 sprites/line, bit5 XRB, bit6 turbo (enables writes to $F3)

vdp_registers.bank_0_scope: Registers 11-15 take effect only in Super Sega mode; in the other modes they are ignored, as on the stock VDP.
vdp_registers.bank_0_evidence: Evidence, not proof (a risk from Technical Reference v2 that v3 keeps): six commercial titles were checked and none write VDP registers 11-15, where Feature Enable A lives. It matters for old code running in Super Sega mode, the only mode in which those registers take effect (bank_0_scope).

bank_1.2: Feature Enable B - bit0 line V-offset, bit1 extended CRAM, bit2 16x16 sprites, bit3 per-sprite collision, bit4 VRAM banking, bits7-6 display height

bits.0: Legacy modes draw from CRAM (12-bit colour in TMS modes)
bits.1: Legacy sprite limit raised from 4 to the Mode 4 limit
bits.4: ESAT extended to 2 bytes per sprite (magnify, early clock)

bank_1.8: Text Window Pattern Base - bits 5-0 = VRAM base >> 8
bank_1.9: Text Window Colours - bits 3-0 foreground palette index, bits 7-4 background

power_on_values.note: Display is OFF at power-on: R1 0xA0 has no display-enable bit. R2 0xFF puts the screen map at 0x3800, R5 0xFF the sprite table at 0x3F00, R6 0xFB the patterns in the first 8 KB.

vdp_registers.xrb_semantics: Extended Register Banks: Feature Enable A (bank 0 R15) bit 5. While it is clear, bits 5-4 of a register-write command are ignored as on stock hardware, and the bank 1-3 registers keep their values but have no effect (Feature Enable B and C read as 0 to the hardware).
vdp_registers.feature_enable_b_height: Feature Enable B bits 7-6: 00 = height from the mode bits, 01 = 224 lines, 10 = 240 lines, 11 = reserved (192). A 224/240 selection by the mode bits takes precedence.

input.controller: Genesis 3-button, TH multiplexed. 0xDC carries port A buttons plus port B up/down; 0xDD carries port B buttons, Reset, CONT and both TH readbacks.

keyboard.enable: Feature Enable C bit 5 on Super Sega; always live in SG-1000 (keyboard attached), SC-3000 and SF-7000 modes

ports.0xDC: PPI port A, input, 8 bits of matrix data
ports.0xDD: PPI port B, input, matrix data in bits 3-0; bits 7,6,5 read 0,1,1 with nothing attached
ports.0xDE: PPI port C, output, row select in bits 2-0 via a 74LS145; bit 3 cassette out; bits 5-7 printer
ports.0xDF: PPI control; not readable, always returns 0xFF

keyboard.polarity: Taken as active low with pull-ups - a pressed key reads 0, an unused matrix position always reads 1. Evidence, not proof: this rests on a single source that contradicts itself (a risk from Technical Reference v2 that v3 keeps). Both implementations use it.
keyboard.rows: 8 groups: rows 0-6 keyboard, row 7 the two gamepads
keyboard.port_c_readback: Reading port C returns its output latch: the last value written, or 0 after a mode word.
keyboard.ghosting: The matrix has no diodes. Two or more keys held on one row make any key on another row sharing those columns read as pressed, and the transpose holds for columns. Real behaviour; modelled and toggleable.
keyboard.common_init: Software writes 0x92 to the control register and 0x07 to port C, configuring A and B as inputs with port C output and selecting row 7 for the gamepads.
keyboard.reset_key: One key raises an NMI on the Z80 rather than appearing in the matrix
keyboard.v5_error: v5 specified row select on port 0x3F bits 2-0 with data on 0xDC bits 6-0 and 0xDD bit 0. That scheme does not exist on hardware.
keyboard.reset_state: The 8255 resets with every port an input. Port C's pull-ups then select row 7, the pads, so SG-1000 software that never touches the PPI still reads its controllers with the keyboard attached.
keyboard.mode_word: Writing a mode word (bit 7 set) to $DF clears the output latches, so port C selects row 0 until software writes it; with bit 7 clear the write sets or clears one port C bit (bit set/reset). Intel 8255A behaviour.

port_3F.bits_7_4: TH/TR output levels: 7 = port B TH, 6 = port B TR, 5 = port A TH, 4 = port A TR
port_3F.bits_3_0: data direction, 1 = input, 0 = output: 3 = port B TH, 2 = port B TR, 1 = port A TH, 0 = port A TR
port_3F.reset_state: 0xFF: every pin an input (bits 3-0 set), level bits 7-4 set
port_3F.region_detection: With TH configured as an output, an export machine reads back the level driven; a Japanese machine always reads 0. This is how software detects region.

mega_drive_mouse.interface: TH-clocked serial on the controller port
mega_drive_mouse.sequence: 4 ID nibbles (0,B,F,F), then sign/overflow, buttons, and two bytes of delta

sports_pad_trackball.interface: TH-clocked, strobe on 0x3F bit 5 for player 1 or bit 7 for player 2
sports_pad_trackball.reports: two 8-bit absolute counters that wrap from 0xFF to 0x00 - not deltas
sports_pad_trackball.sequence: X7-X4 strobe low, X3-X0 strobe high, Y7-Y4 strobe low, Y3-Y0 strobe high
sports_pad_trackball.data: port A bits 3-0, with buttons S1 and S2 on bits 4 and 5
sports_pad_trackball.direction: right increases X, up increases Y
sports_pad_trackball.source: Official Sega Mark III manual, trackball section

pointing_devices.purpose: Computer mode is a mouse and keyboard GUI; the pointer is drawn as a hardware sprite at no per-frame cost
pointing_devices.note: Both share one driver with two device profiles, detected by response pattern.

input.stock_mapping: In the stock modes (Master System, Game Gear, SG-1000, SC-3000) the console presents its Mega Drive pad as that machine's controller: A is button 1 (TL), B is button 2 (TR), and Start is the Game Gear's Start, or the Pause button on the Master System, SG-1000 and SC-3000 (enhancement_layer start_pause, on at power-on). C is used only by the auto-fire boost. A Mega Drive pad plugged into a Master System gives B and C as buttons 1 and 2; the console uses A and B so that the pad's first two buttons are the old consoles' two. Super Sega software reads the pad as a Mega Drive pad (controller). Decided by the owner, October 2026.

audio_control.write: $F2 bits 1-0 select which sound chips are heard: 0 the PSG only (the power-on state), 1 the FM chip only, 2 neither, 3 both
audio_control.read: $F2 returns bits 1-0 of the last value written (bits 7-5 carry a C-sync counter on the Japanese SMS; Super Sega returns 0 there)
audio_control.detection: Software disables the I/O chip ($3E bit 2) before reading $F2 so the controller decode does not drive the bus; the FM latch must still answer.
audio_control.source: MAME sms_m.cpp (smsj_audio_control_r, smsj_set_audio_control); Gearsystem (Audio.h) does the same for Japanese consoles

fm.level: OPEN: the balance of FM and PSG on the original (open question Q20). Both implementations make one FM channel at full volume peak at half a PSG channel at full volume.
fm.write_timing: After an address write to $F0 the chip needs 12 master-clock (base) cycles before the data; after a data write to $F1, 84 before the next write (YM2413 Application Manual). Software leaves this time itself at 100 %; at turbo the bus synchroniser holds the CPU until it has passed (cpu.turbo.fm_writes).

cartridge_slot.sega_mapper_reach: 8-bit bank registers address 256 x 16 KB = 4 MB. The 8 MB slot figure needs a ninth bank bit. OPEN: maximum ROM size and the register layout above 4 MB.

sg1000_carts.mapping: linear, no mapper, 1 KB work RAM mirrored from 0xC000
sg1000_carts.note: SG-1000 and SC-3000 cartridges run natively; the machine selects the legacy memory map when an SG image is loaded.

sega.fffc_bits: 7 ROM-write enable, 4 RAM enable 0xC000-0xFFFF, 3 RAM enable 0x8000-0xBFFF, 2 RAM bank select, 1-0 bank shift
sega.slot_0_protection: the first 1 KB is unaffected by banking, preserving the interrupt vectors
sega.cart_ram_open: The 315-5235 maps 2 x 16 KB of cartridge RAM through $FFFC bits 3 and 2. The emulator models 2 x 8 KB mirrored in the 16 KB window, and the save card format is built on 8 KB windows. OPEN: which size the machine guarantees.

codemasters.registers: 0x0000, 0x4000, 0x8000 exactly (Gearsystem and MAME decode the full address)
codemasters.no_vector_protection: the first 1 KB banks too, so interrupt vectors must be replaced
codemasters.on_cart_ram: high bit written to 0x4000 maps 8 KB at 0xA000-0xBFFF (Ernie Els Golf)
codemasters.note: no RAM mirroring of mapper writes, so the last value cannot be read back
codemasters.v6_error: v6 said any address within a slot acts as its register. No source supports it; with it, a write into the on-cart RAM window's slot would also bank-switch.

korean.registers: 0xA000 exactly selects slot 2; slots 0 and 1 fixed to banks 0 and 1

msx_nemesis.nemesis_variant: last 8 KB bank fixed at 0x0000, second at 0x2000
msx_nemesis.implementation: The emulator and the Pocket core implement the MSX variant only; the Nemesis variant is not implemented yet.

mappers.note: Only a Sega-mapper cartridge has hardware at 0xFFFC-0xFFFF. On the other families those addresses are plain work RAM and must not bank anything.

sc3000_carts.cart_ram: 0x8000-0xBFFF, 16 KB; or 32 KB contiguous 0x8000-0xFFFF with work RAM disabled
sc3000_carts.work_ram: 2 KB only, mirrored every 2 KB across 0xC000-0xFFFF
sc3000_carts.verified_software: Sega Home BASIC v1.0j, Mitec SC-3000 BASIC Level 2 and Level 3 all boot and poll the keyboard
sc3000_carts.v5_error: v5 folded SC-3000 into the SG-1000 map with 1 KB of work RAM and nothing at 0x8000. No 32 KB SC-3000 BASIC can initialise under that map.

sf7000.rom_overlay: With /ROM SEL low the IPL is mapped over 0x0000-0x3FFF, mirrored from 8 KB, but WRITES to that range still land in RAM. Reads see ROM, writes see RAM.

ppi.0xE4: port A, input: FDC and printer status
ppi.0xE6: port C, output: FDD, FDC, ROM mapping, printer
ppi.0xE7: control; /ROM SEL is driven by 8255 bit set/reset, not whole-port writes

sf7000.port_c_bits: 0 FDD /INUSE, 1 FDD /MOTOR ON, 2 FDC TC, 3 FDC RESET, 6 /ROM SEL, 7 printer /STROBE

floppy.geometry: 40 tracks x 16 sectors x 256 bytes = 160 KB
floppy.owner: FPGA, backed by disk images rather than a drive
floppy.rationale: A harvested uPD765 would still need a 3-inch drive and 3-inch media, both scarcer than the controller. Images have no mechanism to fail and are what survives in preservation.

sf7000.source: SF-7000 IPL disassembly; register map and bit assignments are documented, not inferred
sf7000.ppi_mode_word: As on the keyboard PPI, a mode word clears port C, which drives /ROM SEL low and maps the IPL back in.

math_unit.divide_open: UNDER-SPECIFIED. The emulator computes ((A << 8) | B) / B, which is almost certainly not the intent. Proposal: A / B with quotient in $0F and remainder in $10, divide by zero returns $FF/$00. Needs a decision.

compatibility.reset_state: All features disabled, turbo at 100%, legacy modes authentic. Behaviour-identical to stock hardware in every mode.
compatibility.extension_gating: Feature Enable A, B and C; the extended register file behind XRB.
compatibility.sg_software: An unmodified SG-1000 ROM renders with the fixed TMS palette, 4 sprites per line and no line interrupts, exactly as on real hardware, until Feature Enable C bits 0-1 are set. Whether Super Sega software can enable line interrupts in the legacy modes is open question Q15.

implementation_order: 1. CRAM expansion and dual write mode
4. Dual-slot loader, port 0x09, card bank at 0x0B
7. ESAT 2-byte: flip, priority, size, magnify, early clock, palette
9. Window layer, then text window mode
10. Line H and V offset tables, 224/240 heights
11. Legacy mode enhancements: CRAM colour, raised sprite limit, line interrupts (open question Q15)
13. PCM FIFO, math unit, per-sprite collision
14. Multitap protocols, EXT serial link, SC-3000 keyboard
15. TIER 2: extended CRAM, wavetable, VRAM banking, unique-cell mode
17. Card battery SRAM, banked work RAM, lint mode, debugger views
v6_changes: Turbo control moved off port 0x3F. Bits 6-4 there are the TR output levels on real hardware: stock SMS/GG software driving TR would have silently changed the clock, and Super Sega software could never have used both. Turbo is now port 0xF3, gated by Feature Enable A bit 6, outside the 0x00-0x3F mirror range.

Keyboard interface corrected. The SK-1100 is read through the 8255 PPI at 0xDC-0xDF, not via port 0x3F as v5 stated. Row select is PPI port C bits 2-0 at 0xDE; data returns on port A (0xDC, 8 bits) and port B (0xDD, bits 3-0). The v5 scheme does not exist on hardware and real SC-3000 software would not have worked with it.
Full SK-1100 matrix behaviour specified, resolving the v5 note that it must be transcribed during implementation.
Work RAM raised from 8 KB banked to 128 KB in 16 banks of 8 KB, to host SF-7000 compatibility and give native software real headroom.

SC-3000 promoted to its own machine mode. It is not the SG-1000: the cartridge sets the memory map, work RAM is 2 KB mirrored, and the cart supplies RAM at 0x8000. v5 folded it into the SG-1000 map, under which no SC-3000 BASIC can run.
SF-7000 expansion added: 64 KB RAM, 8 KB IPL ROM with a read/write-split overlay, second PPI at 0xE4-0xE7, uPD765-class floppy controller at 0xE0-0xE1.
Bus synchroniser cadence set to the official figures: 16 Z80 T-states in VBLANK, 29 during active video.
Pointing devices added: Mega Drive mouse and Sports Pad trackball, both TH-clocked on the controller port.
Cartridge mapper families specified: Sega, Codemasters, Korean, MSX/Nemesis.
VDP power-on register values specified from the official manual.
Port map conflict with the 0x3E/0x3F mirror scheme documented as an open risk.
Port 0x3E memory enables implemented rather than merely stored. The emulator kept the value and ignored all six bits, so joystick, RAM, cartridge and card disables had no effect.

Display height selection corrected in the emulator to match what this profile already specified: the M1-M4 mode bits in registers 0 and 1. The emulator had only the Super Sega Feature Enable B path, so no SMS or GG title could reach the 224 or 240-line modes. The profile was right and the implementation was not.

Debug facility ports remapped to avoid colliding with the SDSC debug console at 0xFC-0xFD, an established SMS homebrew convention. The FPGA UART now implements SDSC, so existing homebrew debug output works unchanged. FPGA control moved to 0xFB and the watchpoint register file to 0xFE/0xFF.

work_ram.rationale: 128 KB lets the first 64 KB be presented as a contiguous bank set for SF-7000 compatibility, and gives native software real headroom. v5 specified 8 KB banked to 64 KB.
work_ram.stock_compatibility: Bank 0 at reset presents the stock 8 KB an SMS title expects.

vram.expansion_enable: Feature Enable B (bank1 R2) bit 4 enables the 32 KB map; bank1 R3 bit 0 selects the bank the CPU port reaches

port_3E_memory_enables.reset_value: 0xA8: the state of a machine whose BIOS has handed over to a cartridge - cartridge, RAM and controllers enabled; BIOS, card and external port disabled

port_map.mirror_scheme: On SMS hardware every EVEN address 0x00-0x3E mirrors 0x3E and every ODD address 0x01-0x3F mirrors 0x3F. The Game Gear decodes 0x00-0x06 separately for its own registers. On every stock machine the PSG is written at any port in 0x40-0x7F and the VDP answers across 0x80-0xBF (even ports data, odd ports control); on the Master System and Game Gear the V counter reads at every even port and the H counter at every odd port in 0x40-0x7F. The SG-1000, SC-3000 and SF-7000 have no 0x3E/0x3F registers: in those modes writes to 0x00-0x3F do nothing.
port_map.mode_scope: Writes to the Super Sega registers at 0x07-0x16 take effect only in Super Sega mode, as do writes to VDP bank 0 R11-R15 (vdp_registers.bank_0_scope). 0x06 is a register in the Super Sega and Game Gear modes. In every other mode these ports and registers do what they do on the stock machine.
port_map.open_risk: Super Sega registers at 0x06-0x16 sit inside that mirror range and must be decoded specifically, as the Game Gear already does. Because they are decoded only in Super Sega mode (mode_scope), stock software running in its own mode is unaffected. The risk is old code running in Super Sega mode - a retagged or converted title, or a stock cartridge started in Super Sega mode as software_detection option 2 proposes - that writes a mirror address in 0x06-0x16 instead of 0x3E/0x3F: it reaches a Super Sega register instead. Documentation calls mirror use highly unrecommended for homebrew, which implies commercial software does it. NOT YET RESOLVED - candidate fix is to relocate these registers above 0xF0 (open question Q1).

registers.0x00: Game Gear port 0: bit 7 Start (0 = pressed), bit 6 region (1 = export), bits 5-0 read 0. Decoded in Game Gear AND Super Sega modes.
registers.0xC0-0xDF: controllers: 0xDC/0xDD, mirrored across the range; while the SK-1100 keyboard is live (input.keyboard.enable), the PPI at 0xDC-0xDF instead, mirrored across the range
registers.0xF3: turbo step - relocated from 0x3F in v6
registers.0x01-0x05: Game Gear serial / EXT link registers, Game Gear and Super Sega modes
registers.0xFB-0xFF: debug unit (see debug_facility); reads answer only in Super Sega mode

port_map.io_chip_disable: $3E bit 2 disables the controller decode (the $DC/$DD mirror across $C0-$FF) on the Master System and on Super Sega. It has no effect on the Game Gear, even in SMS mode. It does not affect $F2 (FM detection) or Super Sega's fully decoded $F0-$FF window.

super_sega_read_values.0x07-0x16: decoded by the FPGA in Super Sega mode; ports with no readable register return $FF, never the controller mirror
super_sega_read_values.0xFB-0xFF: debug unit: $FB the control value as written; $FC and $FD status (bit 7 debug host attached, bit 6 set, bit 0 trace buffer full); $FE and $FF $FF

fpga_partition.principle: A real 315-5535 ASIC renders the base layer; the FPGA owns everything the ASIC has no register for. Modelling the split explicitly keeps the emulator structurally honest.
fpga_jobs: VDP control-port gating (absorbs bank>=1 writes so they cannot corrupt ASIC registers)
fpga_partition.overlay_capability: Because the FPGA sits in the CPU-to-VDP path it can hold the Z80 and draw over ANY running software, including a commercial cartridge that knows nothing about Super Sega. This is the mechanism for save dialogs, standby, and switching between game and computer mode.

debug_facility.rationale: Four capabilities a debugger running on the Z80 cannot provide, each following from the FPGA sitting on the bus.

ports.0xFB: control: bits 1-0 trace mode, bit 2 arm watchpoint, bit 3 raise overlay, bit 4 clear trace, bit 5 emit marker
ports.0xFC: SDSC console control; value 2 clears the console
ports.0xFE: watchpoint register select bits 2-0; kind in bits 7-6 (VRAM, port, CPU write, CRAM)

debug_facility.watchpoint_fields: address low and high, range end low and high, value to match, flags (bit 0 match value, bit 1 one-shot), ignore count
debug_facility.watchpoint_note: A single address on a busy port such as 0xBE fires tens of thousands of times per second. Range, value match, ignore count and one-shot together reduce that to one meaningful hit.
debug_facility.trace_buffer: FPGA-side, mirrored to FRAM on a fault, so it outlives the crash that destroyed the program state. It is not cleared by a machine reset.
debug_facility.overlay: Composited after the ASIC output, using a font in FPGA memory. Never touches the program VRAM or CRAM, so software cannot detect it happened.
debug_facility.post: Runs before the CPU leaves reset. Ten documented codes; also blinked on the power LED for a machine that cannot reach video.
debug_facility.availability: Writes reach the debug unit in every machine mode, since its purpose is inspecting stock software; stock hardware ignores writes to $FB-$FF. Reads of $FB-$FF answer from the debug unit only in Super Sega mode. In the stock modes they read as on the stock machine (the controller mirror; $FF on the Game Gear), because stock software may read its pads there.
debug_facility.read_values: debug unit: $FB the control value as written; $FC and $FD status (bit 7 debug host attached, bit 6 set, bit 0 trace buffer full); $FE and $FF $FF

stock_behaviour.note: Behaviour of the stock parts that every implementation must reproduce. These are not Super Sega additions; they are listed because the emulator had them wrong until October 2026 and the Pocket core is verified against it.

cpu.halt: An interrupt taken in HALT returns to the instruction after HALT.
cpu.ei: Interrupts are not accepted until the instruction after EI has executed.
cpu.sampling: Maskable interrupts are sampled between instructions.
cpu.index_prefix: DD/FD take a displacement only for the (HL) forms. (IX+d) costs 8 T-states more than (HL); LD (IX+d),n costs 5 more. DDCB: BIT 20, others 23. A prefix followed by another prefix costs 4.

vdp.h_scroll: Screen x = map x + R8 (the background moves right as R8 increases). Latched once per line before the line is drawn; R0 bit 6 exempts rows 0-1.
vdp.v_scroll: R9 is latched once per frame; a write takes effect from the next frame.
vdp.sprite_y: A sprite starts on line Y+1. When Y+1 is 241-256 it starts at Y+1-256 instead, so Y = $F0-$FF shows its lower rows at the top of the screen (Gearsystem and MAME; a plain 8-bit compare would differ only for 32-line magnified sprites at Y = $E0-$EF).
vdp.extra_height: 224/240-line modes use a 32x32 name table at (R2 bits 3-2) x $1000 + $700, the map wraps at 256 lines instead of 224, and $D0 no longer ends the sprite list.

event_timing.note: Within the 228-cycle line, these happen at fixed cycle offsets (Gearsystem's model, which passes the SMS VDP test ROMs). The machine uses the 315-5535 column.
event_timing.line_render: 195 / 186 (background of this line, sprites of the next)
event_timing.collision_flag: 20 / 22 + X x 228 / 256 of the line after the sprites were drawn, or at the render event if that comes first (Gearsystem drops such late collisions; the hardware flags a collision anywhere on the line)
event_timing.io_access_point: IN/OUT reach the port 10 T-states into the instruction (IN A,(n), OUT (n),A)

v_counter.source: Charles MacDonald, Sega Master System VDP documentation (which lists NTSC 240 as 00-FF, 00-06: 263 values for a 262-line frame; the implementations use 00-05)

vdp.h_counter: 00-93 then E9-FF, one count per two pixels; latched on a TH edge for the light gun.
vdp.frame_flag: Status bit 7 is set at cycle 25 (SMS2) / 27 (315-5535) of line height + 1, the second line after the last displayed one, and stays set until the status register is read.
vdp.line_counter: On lines 0 to height inclusive (one line past the display) the counter counts down; on reaching 0 it reloads from R10 and raises the line interrupt. On other lines it is reloaded from R10. Mode 4 only as stock (TMS modes raise no line interrupt); whether Super Sega runs it in the TMS modes is open question Q15.
vdp.line_timing: 228 CPU cycles per line, 262 lines NTSC, 313 PAL; the overrun of the last instruction of a line belongs to the next line.

psg.tone: Counters run at CPU/16 and toggle the output on reaching zero; a period of 0 behaves as 1.
psg.noise: The noise counter (rate $10/$20/$40 or tone 2) toggles a flip-flop; the 16-bit shift register advances on its rising edge, once per two counter periods. White noise taps bits 0 and 3; writing the noise register resets the register to $8000.
psg.volume: Attenuation 2 dB per step; 15 is silent.

io.low_port_reads: Reads of $00-$3F return $FF on the Master System, and on the Game Gear and Super Sega for every port they do not decode as a register.
io.tr_readback: A TR pin configured as an output ($3F bit 0 or 2 clear) reads back the level driven: $DC bit 5 for port A, $DD bit 3 for port B.
io.game_gear_decode: Above $C0 the Game Gear answers only $C0/$DC (port A) and $C1/$DD (port B, with bits 7-6 = $3F bits 7-6); every other port reads $FF, $F2 included (no FM).
io.fm_latch: The $F2 FM detection latch answers in Master System and Super Sega modes only.

stock_behaviour.verification: Batman Returns (Europe) SMS in PAL at frames 30, 60, 120, 200, 500, 900 and 1500, and Batman Returns (World) GG at frames 200, 500, 900 and 1500: the emulator and the Pocket core RTL (Verilator) both match Gearsystem, Game Gear within Gearsystem's colour rounding (it expands channel value 5 to 86 rather than 85). Plus VDP test ROMs at 192/224/240 lines (October 2026).

software_detection.question: How does one ROM tell, at run time, that it is on a Super Sega? Extended features are reachable only in Super Sega mode, which the header region (8) selects, and an export SMS BIOS refuses region 8. A single ROM for both machines therefore cannot use region 8.
options: Two ROMs from one source (what the Super Mario Land DX port does now).
A boot-menu option to run a region-4 cartridge in Super Sega mode, plus a read-only machine ID register the ROM can test.
An unlock sequence that switches a running region-4 title into Super Sega mode.
software_detection.source: Super Mario Land DX port design, distribution question

modding.machine_side: Computer mode can apply a BPS patch to a cartridge image while writing a blank card, which is how a mod reaches real hardware. The console plays mods; it does not make them.
modding.not_machine: Making mods (the ROM hack maker and its plugins) is emulator-only.
modding.distribution: Mods are distributed only as BPS patches.
modding.source: Golden Axe / ROM hack maker work (October 2026)

enhancement_layer.purpose: Optional boosts for unmodified SG-1000, SC-3000, Master System and Game Gear software, applied by intercepting the fixed hardware interfaces (VDP ports, PSG, pads) rather than patching the ROM. Full rationale and tiers: SuperSega_AutoEnhancement_Layer.md (the "AEL doc" below), an earlier design document that is not in this repository.
enhancement_layer.default: Every boost but two is off at power-on, so the machine behaves as stock hardware: True TMS colours starts on, so SG-1000 and SC-3000 software shows the colours it was made for (Q11), and Start = Pause starts on, because the console's pad has no Pause button (input.stock_mapping). Each one is switched independently: on the console from the boot menu, in the emulator from its AEL panel, on the Analogue Pocket core from the core settings (Interact) menu.
enhancement_layer.precedence: Explicit software intent wins. Every boost acts only on software running in the stock modes (SG-1000, SC-3000, Master System, Game Gear): Super Sega software sets these features itself and reads C as a button of its own. Pseudo-stereo also stops once software writes $06. Start = Pause applies in the Master System, SG-1000 and SC-3000 modes (the Game Gear has a Start button of its own). The TMS colour boost is the one exception: it also acts on Super Sega software's TMS modes (Q11).

boosts.sprite_limit: 16 sprites per line instead of 8 in Mode 4, and instead of 4 in the TMS modes.
boosts.overflow_stock: With the raised limit, status bit 6 is still set by a 9th sprite on a line, for software that reads it as logic. Mode 4 only: in the TMS modes it has no effect.
boosts.start_pause: Start on the pad raises the Pause NMI (SMS, SG-1000, SC-3000 modes). On at power-on.
boosts.turbo: A turbo step (125-200 %) for stock software in the SMS, GG, SG-1000 and SC-3000 modes. Super Sega software sets its own step through $F3.
boosts.vram_boost: No VDP access wait (bus synchroniser bypassed) while a turbo step is active.
boosts.autofire: While C is held, button 2 repeats: it toggles every two frames (15 Hz at 60 Hz). The pad state itself is not changed, so releasing C leaves button 2 as the pad has it.
boosts.pseudo_stereo: Until software writes $06, the PSG is panned tone 0 left, tone 1 right, tone 2 and noise centre (the $06 value $DE).
boosts.gg_uncrop: Game Gear software is shown at the full 256x192 instead of the 160x144 window.
boosts.tms_colour: SG-1000/SC-3000 picture modes use true TMS9918 colours instead of the Master System approximation.
boosts.fm_present: Inherent to the machine (the FM unit is always fitted), not a switch.

enhancement_layer.not_modelled: "VRAM write reliability" (AEL doc, tier 1) has no switch: the emulator and the Pocket core never drop a VDP write, so they already behave as if it were on.
enhancement_layer.region_speed: "Region speed correction" (AEL doc, tier 1) is the machine's 50/60 Hz video setting (the emulator's PAL switch, the Pocket core's Video setting), not a separate boost.

open_questions.detail: Registers $06-$16 sit in the $3E/$3F mirror range. Stock software in its own mode is unaffected (port_map.mode_scope); the risk is old code running in Super Sega mode - a retagged or converted title, or a stock cartridge started in Super Sega mode (software_detection option 2) - that writes a $3E/$3F mirror address in $06-$16. Relocation above $F0 is the candidate fix.

open_questions.topic: Maximum ROM size and mapper layout above 4 MB
open_questions.detail: See media.cartridge_slot.sega_mapper_reach.
See media.mappers.sega.cart_ram_open.

open_questions.topic: ESAT entry format; H-flip per sprite or per tile
open_questions.detail: 2 bytes per sprite; byte 0 bit 1 H-flip, bit 0 V-flip, per sprite.

open_questions.topic: Unique-cell mode and 32 KB VRAM: coupled or independent
open_questions.detail: Coupled: unique-cell mode requires VRAM expansion (Feature Enable B bit 4).
Off at reset. A title enables it itself (Feature Enable A bit 6, then $F3). The enhancement layer's turbo boost is for unmodified software in the stock modes and does not apply to Super Sega titles.
See math_unit.divide_open.
See software_detection.
Not readable today. Interrupt handlers that switch banks need to restore the previous one; readback or a documented RAM shadow is needed.
A hack-maker workflow, not a machine question; listed so it is not lost.

open_questions.topic: Default of the TMS colour boost
open_questions.detail: Decided by the owner in October 2026: true TMS9918 colours are on at power-on, the one exception to every boost starting off, and the boost also acts on the TMS modes of Super Sega software. The emulator already did both; the Pocket core does the same.

cpu.turbo.cartridge_wait gives one wait state per cartridge access at 200 % (250 ns ROM). The emulator applies it; the Pocket core does not yet (its PSRAM answers in time). Affects only software running at 200 %.

ESAT has been 2 bytes per sprite since v5, and v6 confirmed it (Q4), but Feature Enable C bit 4 still selects a 2-byte mode and the emulator implements a 1-byte layout when it is clear. Retire the bit, or document the 1-byte layout.

$08 bits 6-4 report the fill of a 64-byte FIFO, which three bits cannot encode: the emulator returns the fill modulo 8, so a full FIFO reads as empty. Proposal: bits 6-4 = bytes queued / 8, saturating at 7.

open_questions.topic: Line interrupts in the TMS9918 (legacy) modes
open_questions.detail: v5 made line interrupts in the legacy modes a Super Sega enhancement (video.legacy_modes.enhancements.line_interrupts), but no enable bit was ever assigned; as stock, TMS modes raise none (stock_behaviour.vdp.line_counter), and both implementations follow that in the stock modes. In Super Sega mode both raise them in the TMS modes whenever R0 bit 4 is set. Should the line counter run in the legacy modes on Super Sega, and what enables it?

open_questions.topic: Register layouts defined only by the emulator
open_questions.detail: The bit layouts of the DMA engine ($F4-$FA), PCM control ($08 write), the wavetable ($11-$15), slot select ($09), the VDP base registers (bank 0 R11 and R12, bank 1 R0, R1, R5 and R6) and the window split (bank 0 R13 and R14) are defined today only by the emulator's implementation (the Pocket core already follows it for $09). They need writing into the profile and the Technical Reference, and checking, before the Pocket core implements them, as v7 did for the math unit.

open_questions.topic: Feature Enable B height in the TMS modes
open_questions.detail: Feature Enable B bits 7-6 select 224 or 240 lines for Super Sega software, but the documents define the heights only for Mode 4. Both implementations also apply them while a TMS9918 mode is selected. Should the machine apply them in the TMS modes, and if so, what do those modes draw below line 192?

open_questions.topic: TMS-mode status bits 4-0 and transparent sprites
open_questions.detail: Two details of the sprite flags in the TMS modes are not settled for this VDP. (1) What status bits 4-0 read: the TMS9918A puts the number of the fifth sprite there; Gearsystem does that whenever a TMS mode is selected (not on the Game Gear) and reads $1F in Mode 4; the Pocket core reads $1F and the emulator 0 in every mode. (2) Whether a transparent (colour 0) sprite takes part in collisions: the TMS9918A Data Manual says it does; Gearsystem, the emulator and the Pocket core leave it out.

open_questions.topic: Several TMS mode bits set at once
open_questions.detail: The implementations take M2 (Graphics II) first, then M1 (Text), then M3 (Multicolor); Gearsystem takes M1, then M3, then M2; on the TMS9918A such combinations give undocumented hybrid modes. Which picture should the machine show?

How loud the FM chip is beside the PSG on the original Japanese Master System, where the two are mixed in analogue, is not known: MAME gives both chips the same gain, Gearsystem lowers the PSG to 0.8 while both play, and neither cites a measurement. Both implementations make one FM channel at full volume peak at half a PSG channel at full volume. The chip also has separate melody and rhythm outputs, whose mix on the console's board is not known either; the Pocket core uses IKAOPLL's default weights (2 and 3), and the emulator has no rhythm instruments. What balance should the machine have?

The YM2413 needs 12 master-clock cycles after an address write and 84 after a data write before it takes the next write. Software written for 100 % spaces its writes by CPU time, so at turbo steps above 100 % they can come too close: on the Pocket core a test driver that leaves the chip little more than the minimum at 100 % played no FM at 200 %. Decided by the owner in October 2026: at turbo the bus synchroniser holds the CPU on a write to $F0/$F1 until the chip can take it, as it does for the VDP (cpu.turbo.fm_writes). Both implementations do this.

The turbo steps are defined at the NTSC clock: 4.47, 5.37, 6.26 and 7.16 MHz. In PAL both implementations run the same percentages of the PAL clock, 4.434, 5.320, 6.207 and 7.094 MHz, because their turbo is a multiple of the base clock. Should PAL turbo be those, or the NTSC frequencies?
